title: Minimax Causal Value Estimation When Treatment and a Binary Event Vanish Together
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield below field floor; paper_score_ceiling=7.3 < 7.4 and salvageable=false within scope; math referee PASS after proof-local repair.
gap_reasons: The result is confined to a highly structured law class: uniform covariates, an exactly known polynomial propensity, zero control potential outcomes, and a power-form treated Bernoulli mean with a fixed positive Lipschitz remainder
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a finite-sample all-estimator minimax risk envelope for the known polynomial-propensity Bernoulli edge model, including an attaining estimator, the moving critical crossover, and constant-factor adaptation to unknown beta. After a local proof-reference repair, the math referee passed with no findings. The field-tier novelty case failed: the general reviewer assigned subfield with a 7.3 score ceiling below the 7.4 field threshold and no bounded same-scope repair; the decision reviewer also requested an accepted-bank comparison to a result that is actually banked downgraded.
tldr: For a known polynomial propensity \(e_{\alpha,c}(x)=cx^\alpha\), a full causal value can remain point identified while its optimal MSE is nonparametric because treatment and a binary event vanish together.  Uniformly over \(\alpha\in[3/2,5/2]\), \(c\in[1/4,1]\), and \(\beta\in[1/2,3/2]\), the matched all-estimator risk is \(S_{n,\alpha,\beta}/n\), where \(h=n^{-1/(\alpha+\beta+3)}\) and \(S=1+\int_h^1x^{\beta-\alpha}\,dx\).  An explicit boundary estimator attains it, and a beta-free count-selected version attains every oracle rate within a universal constant, so unknown-exponent adaptation has no rate penalty.
gap: General modulus theory explains how to obtain minimax bounds. Fixed-design normal-regression ATE work optimizes linear-estimator RMSE under smooth conditional means, and trimmed-IPW work derives estimator-specific limit laws under regular variation and a nondegenerate boundary outcome distribution. None of these results supplies a matched all-estimator calculation for a full value when conditional Bernoulli variance vanishes at the same boundary as treatment overlap.
fill: The project evaluates the Bernoulli information modulus directly, verifies a positive Lipschitz least-favorable pair, and constructs a closed-form estimator that extrapolates the smooth remainder from a deterministic boundary bin.
